They also allege that the Thai government is intentionally delaying Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) talks following the February election.
title: Thai actions at border a 'calculated annexation strategy'

summary: นายกฯ อนุทิน ออกมาเช็คข่าวกับเสธ. ทบ. แล้ว ยืนยันว่าสถานการณ์ชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชายังปกติ ไม่มีอะไรน่าเป็นห่วง ที่เห็นทหารกัมพูชาขยับตัวก็แค่การเคลื่อนย้ายกำลังพลตามวงรอบธรรมดา ไม่ได้เตรียมปะทะอะไร นายกฯ ฝากบอกประชาชนว่าไม่ต้องกังวลและให้สบายใจได้เลย
title: นายกฯ ย้ำ ชายแดนกัมพูชาไม่มีอะไรน่าห่วง เสธ ทบ.รายงานแค่เคลื่อนย้ายกำลังพลตามปกติ ขอให้สบายใจได้

summary: The Army spokesperson confirmed that while they are monitoring every Cambodian move, no immediate factors for a third round of war have been found. However, he noted there is 'no guarantee' for the future and the military remains fully prepared. Public concern has risen following reports of Cambodian troop accumulation.
title: Thai Army insists border situation shows no factors for Round 3 combat

summary: This report analyzes the likelihood of a third conflict following intense July 2025 fighting. It notes Thailand's technological advantage with F-16s and AI-integrated suicide drones, while Cambodia focuses on accumulating Eastern European armaments. Cumulative losses for Thailand since 2025 stand at 46 personnel, with over 800,000 civilians displaced during the height of the crisis.
title: Rumors of a Third Round of Fighting: Comparing Troop Strength and Heavy Weapons

summary: The Royal Thai Navy inspected the border at Ban Hat Lek in Trat province and reported that a Cambodian silt-trap dam has caused Thailand to lose over 3,000 square meters of land due to coastal changes, while Cambodia gained 30,000 square meters. Although 127 meters of the dam were removed following past clashes, the Navy demands deeper excavation to restore the ecosystem. Border forces remain on high alert for security threats like weapons and narcotics trafficking.
title: Thai Navy urges Cambodia to remove more of 'silt-trap dam' in Trat, citing 3,000 sq m of Thai land loss

summary: The Cambodian Border Affairs Secretariat issued a statement firmly rejecting a Thai Senate committee's recommendation to revoke the 2000 Memorandum of Understanding (MoU 43) on border affairs. Cambodia argues that the move is politically motivated, lacks legal grounds, and violates international law regarding the inviolability of borders. Phnom Penh insists on using existing bilateral mechanisms like the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) to resolve disputes.
title: Cambodia rejects Thai Senate's call to scrap border MoU 2000

source: MGR Online (ผู้จัดการออนไลน์)
summary: Cambodia has warned Thailand that unilaterally canceling the 2000 Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on land boundaries would be a violation of the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties. Cambodian officials argue that the agreement is essential for peaceful dispute resolution and that the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) has already made progress in marking 74 border points. This comes as a response to growing calls within the Thai Senate to scrap the pact.
title: Cambodia warns Thailand not to cancel MOU 2000, claiming it endangers peace and violates international law

summary: The Commander of the 11th Infantry Division visited the Thai-Cambodian border in Sa Kaeo Province on March 26, 2026, to oversee the adjustment of troop deployments. The move aims to ensure efficiency and combat readiness in line with the current situation to maintain national security and safety along the border.
title: Thai 1st Army Region adjusts troop positions in Sa Kaeo, ready for combat

summary: The Thai Navy has increased patrols along maritime boundaries after detecting 20-30 armed Cambodian fishing vessels entering Thai waters. Reports indicate these vessels are involved in harassing Thai fishermen and illegally transporting Thai seafood back to Cambodia. Authorities have already seized several shipments and are maintaining a strict watch to prevent further incursions.
title: Navy tightens control over Thai waters, monitoring 'armed Cambodian fishing gangs' causing trouble

summary: Thai Marines in Trat province have increased monitoring following reports of gunfire and 'intermittent provocations' from the Cambodian side over the past week. Captain Thammanoon Wanna suggested a change in Cambodian local leadership might be causing the friction. The disputed Thmor Da area is reportedly under Thai control but remains a hotspot for Chinese-backed scam operations.
title: Thai forces warn of new provocations along border

summary: Phnom Penh has officially dismissed a recommendation from a Thai Senate committee to revoke the 2000 Memorandum of Understanding (MOU 2000) regarding land boundaries. Cambodian officials labeled the move as 'politically motivated' and warned that dismantling this legal framework could lead to a military confrontation. This follows a unanimous vote by a Thai Senate panel on March 24 to scrap the pact, citing concerns over sovereignty and mapping.
title: Cambodia rejects Thai Senate's call to scrap border MoU

summary: A Thai marine commander has accused Cambodian forces of provocations along the Trat border, reporting gunfire heard over the past week as a breach of the December ceasefire. He noted that Thai troops have fortified positions with barbed wire near Ban Sam Lang and are monitoring new Cambodian trenches. He also alleged that parts of the Thmor Da area are being used as a scam hub by Chinese financiers.
title: Thai marine commander warns over alleged ceasefire breaches

summary: Social activist 'Gun Jompalang' reported a tense situation at the border where approximately 40 armed Cambodian soldiers approached Thai lines. While the Cambodian side claimed they intended to negotiate, the presence of weapons caused concern for Thai officers on site. The activist emphasized that the tension was initiated by the Cambodian side moving personnel and weapons close to Thai territory.
title: Gun Jompalang reports tense encounter as armed Cambodian troops approach Thai border

summary: The Royal Thai Navy (RTN) has downplayed the naval threat from Cambodia, stating its capabilities remain low. Officials are currently monitoring the delivery of Chinese-made corvettes to Cambodia. A commander noted that during recent border clashes, the HTMS Thepha was deployed to provide illumination and fire support at Ban Sam Lang to counter Cambodian 130mm artillery threats near Koh Yor, which could reach Thai territory.
title: Thai Navy asserts Cambodian naval power is low, not a threat; monitors Chinese corvette delivery

summary: รองนายกฯ ปรัก สุคน ของกัมพูชา พาคณะทูตต่างชาติและตัวแทนจาก UN ลงไปดูพื้นที่แถวชายแดนจังหวัดโพธิสัตว์ โดยอ้างว่าทหารไทยเข้าไปยึดครองแถมยังตั้งตู้คอนเทนเนอร์และรั้วลวดหนามแบบผิดกฎหมาย นอกจากนี้ยังได้แวะไปเยี่ยมและให้กำลังใจชาวบ้านที่ต้องหนีภัยจากการปะทะกันจำนวน 76 ครอบครัวด้วย
title: กัมพูชานำคณะทูต-UNลงพื้นที่ชายแดนโพธิสัตว์ อ้างไทยยึดครองผิดกฎหมาย

summary: The Royal Thai Army (RTA) spokesperson countered Cambodian claims regarding the number of displaced persons at the border, calling the figures 'exaggerated' and 'distorted.' The RTA maintains that these individuals are intruders violating Thai sovereignty. The Army clarified that barbed wire and containers were deployed to control areas according to ceasefire agreements, not to block civilians from returning home.
title: Army rejects Cambodia's 'distorted' migrant data, insists they are sovereignty intruders

summary: กองทัพเรือไทยกำลังเฝ้าระวังอย่างหนัก หลังพบกองเรือประมงกัมพูชาที่อาจติดอาวุธกว่า 20-30 ลำ ลุกล้ำเข้ามาในน่านน้ำไทยแถวอ่าวไทย โดยคาดว่าน่าจะเข้ามาลอบขนส่งปลาแซลมอนและสินค้าทะเลกลับไปกัมพูชา ทหารเรือจึงต้องคุมเข้มและลาดตระเวนเพื่อปกป้องอธิปไตยทางทะเลของเรา
title: จับตา! กัมพูชาส่งกองเรือประมงติดอาวุธล่วงล้ำอ่าวไทย ทัพเรือไทยคุมเข้มสกัดลอบขนสินค้า

summary: Business sectors are urging the new Anutin 2 government to reverse the hardline approach that caused nearly 1 million Cambodian workers to flee Thailand since mid-2025. The exodus, driven by nationalist tensions and border conflict, has caused a massive labor shortage that Myanmar and Lao workers cannot fill. The editorial argues that the ban on Cambodian labor hurts Thai businesses and encourages illegal crossings, suggesting that economic security is just as vital as border security.
title: Editorial: Let Cambodian Workers Return to Fix Labor Shortage

summary: กองกำลังบูรพากำลังเร่งเก็บกู้ทุ่นระเบิดแถวชายแดนสระแก้ว บริเวณบ้านหนองจาน ล่าสุดเคลียร์พื้นที่ปลอดภัยไปได้เกือบ 40,000 ตารางเมตรแล้ว และยังขุดเจอระเบิดสังหารบุคคล POMZ-2 ด้วย เจ้าหน้าที่ฝากเตือนชาวบ้านให้ระวังให้ดี เพราะยังมีพื้นที่อันตรายเหลืออยู่อีกตั้งกว่า 60%
title: เร่งกู้ทุ่นระเบิดชายแดนสระแก้ว เผยพื้นที่เสี่ยงยังเหลือกว่า 60,000 ตร.ม.

summary: Cambodia has accused Thailand of violating its sovereignty and reportedly invited a group of diplomats to the Thmodar area (adjacent to Trat province) to inspect Thai military activities, including the raising of flags and the installation of barricades. As of the report, the Thai government has not issued a formal official statement, but the situation is being closely monitored by local media as it could impact bilateral relations.
title: Cambodia Claims Thailand Violated Sovereignty, Takes Diplomats to Thmodar to Inspect Border Barricades

summary: The Royal Thai Army (RTA) has rejected allegations from Phnom Penh that Thai troops are preventing tens of thousands of displaced Cambodians from returning to their homes. RTA spokesman Maj Gen Winthai Suvaree called the claims 'grossly exaggerated,' stating only a few thousand people are affected in Sa Kaeo province. He defended the use of barbed wire and shipping containers as temporary measures to maintain stability following recent clashes, consistent with the December 27 ceasefire.
title: Army denies blocking return of displaced

summary: Local reports from Surin province indicate a temporary calm in border districts like Phanom Dong Rak. Residents who previously fled tensions are returning to normal life, with many parents traveling over 100km to enroll their children in secondary schools. Despite the calm, locals remain concerned about high fuel prices and rumors of potential future clashes after the rainy season.
title: Border quietens down as parents rush to enroll children in famous schools

summary: The Royal Thai Navy addressed Cambodian claims that Thailand's placement of shipping containers and barbed wire along the border violates sovereignty. Rear Admiral Paraj Ratanajaipan stated these are defensive measures prompted by 'ill-intentioned individuals' destroying previous barriers. The Navy claims the placement follows the 2025 Joint Statement to maintain current troop positions and prevent further clashes.
title: Thai Navy insists border containers are for 'self-defense'

source: Bangkok Biz News (กรุงเทพธุรกิจ)
summary: Admiral Phairoj Fuangchan, Commander-in-Chief of the Royal Thai Navy, addressed the ongoing tension at the Thmor Da border in Trat Province. He admitted that Cambodian movements appear to have 'hidden objectives' that Thailand cannot yet clearly evaluate. He emphasized a policy of patience to avoid escalation and confirmed that Thai forces remain strictly behind the 'Troop Deployment Line' (TDL) agreed upon on December 27, 2025. Regarding the use of shipping containers, he stated they are only placed in specific high-risk areas to protect Thai personnel from provocations, such as previous incidents where Cambodian individuals dismantled barbed wire and approached Thai troops.
title: Navy Chief Reveals Cambodia's 'Thmor Da' Provocations Have Hidden Motives, Confirms Container Placement Only in Risky Spots

summary: Thai media reported on footage released by Cambodian sources showing Thai soldiers preventing Cambodian monks and individuals from entering Ta Kwai Temple. The 2nd Army Region of Thailand clarified that the temple remains under Thai supervision and urged citizens not to share photos or videos of military equipment movements for national security. This follows viral claims that Cambodia had retaken the site, which Thai authorities deny, stating they are maintaining their positions according to current security protocols.
title: Cambodian Video Shows Thai Soldiers Blocking Entry to Ta Kwai Temple
